findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JS (XSS) and used as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` injects an attacker-controlled header directly inside a JavaScript single-quoted string without escaping. A referer containing `'` (e.g. `http://x/'+alert(1)+'`) breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JS in the Discourse origin. Additionally, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin, not a full URL with path/query; derive the scheme+host (e.g. from SiteSetting.embeddable_host) and escape it with `j`/`to_json`.

findings.title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML as cooked output
findings.body: When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` verbatim, bypassing the sanitizing render pipeline. Content fed through TopicEmbed/PollFeed comes from remote RSS feeds or Readability-scraped pages, so any `<script>`/`onerror=` in the feed is persisted as `cooked` and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic views, giving stored XSS. The HTML must be sanitized (whitelist tags/attrs) before storing.

findings.title: Invalid ERB/Ruby `<%- end if %>` breaks the template
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` which is a Ruby syntax error (a bare `if` with no condition following `end`). Rendering embed/best will raise at template compile time, so the whole embed feature fails. It should be just `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: `force: true` on create_table drops an existing table and its data
findings.body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means the migration issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. On any installation where this migration already ran (or is re-run), existing top_topics data is silently destroyed. The same pattern is used in the new 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds migration, where re-running would drop all embed mappings. Remove `force: true`.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check using indexOf
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL (e.g. origin `http://d` matches `http://discourse.example.com/`), and an empty origin also passes. Compare the message origin against the exact iframe origin instead.

findings.title: poll_feed crashes when a feed item has no `content`
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. For plain RSS 2.0 feeds SimpleRSS exposes `description` and `content` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole scheduled job (retry is disabled, so all items are skipped). Fall back to `i.description`/guard against nil. Also `feed_key` is defined but never used, so the HTTP modified-check it implies does not happen.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "...imported from..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller (PollFeed item content, Readability doc content). This mutates caller state, raises RuntimeError on frozen strings, and causes the footer to be appended repeatedly if the same string is passed to import more than once (changing the content_sha1 and triggering spurious revisions). Build a new string instead.

findings.title: Rails 3 lockfile not updated for new gems
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but Gemfile_rails3.lock was not updated. Booting/bundling in RAILS3 mode (still supported per the Gemfile) will fail with an out-of-date lockfile in deployment/frozen bundles.

findings.title: Full feed poll executed synchronously inside the retrieve path
findings.body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` downloads and imports the entire RSS feed inline whenever a single embed URL is missed. For large feeds this makes the retrieve job long-running and can duplicate work across concurrent retrievals (the redis throttle is per embed_url, not per feed).

findings.title: Embed view renders post.cooked with `raw` for imported HTML posts
findings.body: `<%= raw post.cooked %>` outputs post HTML unescaped. Combined with the new raw_html cook method (which stores remote feed HTML unsanitized), scripts from third-party feeds execute inside the Discourse-origin iframe. Sanitize cooked content for raw_html posts before output.
